items.title: The Pulse Beneath the Job Title: Monthly Readings of Requirements and Tasks from 750 Million Chinese Job Ads
items.desc: Builds catalogs of 20,721 hiring requirements and 44,479 tasks from 752.6 million Chinese job ads (2022-2026), scoring each task for how far a language model could absorb it. Counting occupations suggests LLM-exposed work is vanishing; counting tasks suggests far less of it is. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-08-28]

items.title: CIFQA: A Deterministic Tool-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Financial Query Answering
items.desc: Separates language understanding from numerical execution by assigning specialized LLM agents to interpretation, routing, parameter extraction and planning, while deterministic Python tools do the arithmetic. Reaches 95.5% accuracy on calculation-intensive fixed-deposit queries, with a 17B open backbone beating much larger frontier models. [arXiv q-fin.CP / cs.AI, posted 2026-08-28]

items.title: Graph-Based Modeling of Financial Volatility Dynamics
items.desc: Proposes FA-GSTN, a finance-aware graph spatio-temporal network that treats the implied-volatility surface as an evolving graph rather than a static image. Reports state-of-the-art realized-volatility forecasts (R² up to 0.473) and beats Vision Transformer baselines when trained on only one year of data. [arXiv q-fin.ST, posted 2026-08-28]

items.title: Option-Implied Signals and Crash Risk: Predictability and Machine-Learning Evidence from U.S. Equity Options
items.desc: Re-estimates canonical option-implied return predictability on 12.36 million firm-day observations across three regimes, finding the volatility smirk effect decays to insignificance by 2023-2026. A boosted-tree benchmark only beats linear models in the AI/mega-cap regime, where no hand-engineered signal enters the top five predictors. [arXiv q-fin.ST, posted 2026-08-28]

items.title: Forecasting Economically Significant Bitcoin Moves: A Multi-Scale TCN with Profit-Optimized Thresholds
items.desc: Uses a multi-scale temporal convolutional network with InceptionTCN blocks and channel attention to predict whether Bitcoin will rise more than 5% within seven days, trained on on-chain, market and sentiment data from 2018-2025. Outperforms LSTM, TCN, XGBoost and Random Forest baselines on AUC and simulated profit. [arXiv q-fin.ST, posted 2026-08-28]

items.title: A Statistical-Finance Benchmark for Same-Day Directional Stock Prediction: Walk-Forward Evidence from SPY
items.desc: Benchmarks XGBoost against Random Forest, LightGBM and logistic regression for predicting SPY's same-day close direction using only open-price information, under expanding-window walk-forward validation over 1993-2024. Finds detectable directional signal but cautions that sample-size accounting limits the economic claims. [arXiv q-fin.ST, posted 2026-08-28]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: Federal Reserve officials are debating AI's effect on the economy and jobs
items.desc: A Post analysis of Fed meeting records finds officials repeatedly weighing how AI is reshaping growth, inflation and employment, with Chair Kevin Warsh betting on an AI-driven productivity boom while the Dallas Fed argues large job losses are unlikely this decade. The piece highlights how thin the evidence base still is relative to demand for certainty. [Washington Post, published 2026-08-29]
